cards.text: Psalm 148 opens with one word: "Hallelujah!" Then the psalm writer starts calling out, one after another, who should praise the LORD. Friend, this man has a LIST, and he reads it like the front desk at the busiest office in the world. NEXT!

cards.question: Every list has to start somewhere. Where does the psalm writer first call for praise to come from?
Up in the heavens, the first ones the psalm writer calls on to praise the LORD are all His ___.

cards.text: After the angels and all His heavenly hosts, he calls out to the lights in the sky: "Praise Him, O sun and moon; praise Him, all you shining stars." He's talking to the SUN, friend, and I talk to my oven every single morning, so who am I to judge?

cards.question: After the sun, moon and stars, the psalm writer is done with the sky. Nothing higher gets called on to praise the LORD.

cards.text: He goes even higher: "Praise Him, O highest heavens, and you waters above the skies." This man is checking the TOP shelf, friend, the one even I can't reach, and I've got a gold base AND a tall hat.

cards.question: Everything up in the heavens is called to praise the name of the LORD. What reason does the psalm writer give?

answers.text: He commanded and they were created
They were made to serve people
They live closest to His throne

cards.question: God doesn't just make the heavens and walk away. He sets them in place to last ___.

cards.text: "He issued a decree that will never pass away." Friend, I shared a junk drawer with an expired coupon for YEARS, so a decree that NEVER runs out sounds like a miracle to me.

cards.question: The heavens are covered, from the angels all the way up to the highest heavens. Where does the psalm writer call for praise to come from next?

cards.text: He starts at the bottom: all great sea creatures and the ocean depths. Way down in the dark, friend, and they still get called up, and believe me, I KNOW how good that feels.

cards.question: Next on the earth's list is the weather. What does the psalm writer say the powerful wind is doing?

cards.text: Lightning and hail, snow and clouds, the whole forecast gets called on. My weather app sees that lineup and sends me ELEVEN alerts, friend, but the psalm writer sees it and hands them a HYMNAL.

cards.question: On the earth, the psalm writer calls on the mountains and hills to praise the LORD, but the trees don't make the list.

cards.text: Mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars, wild animals and all cattle, crawling creatures and flying birds. Friend, the CEDARS got called up before me, and I'm the one wearing the tall hat.

cards.question: After the animals, the psalm writer finally gets to people. Who's at the top of that list?

answers.text: Kings and rulers of the earth

cards.text: Kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all rulers of the earth. The folks who run the world get called right after the cattle, friend, and NO crown gets you a better seat in THIS choir.

cards.question: When the psalm writer calls on people to praise the LORD, he calls the old and the young separately, one group at a time.

cards.text: Young men and maidens, old and young together. Grandpa and the grandkid singing the same song, friend, that's a duet I'd buy a ticket to, and I don't even have POCKETS.

cards.question: The earth gets the same line the heavens got: "Let them praise the name of the LORD". This time the reason is that His name is the ___ name that is exalted.

cards.text: His splendor is above the earth and the heavens, and then the psalm turns to His people: He has raised up a horn for them, the praise of all His saints. Friend, after a list THAT long I was sure somebody got forgotten, but take it from a stamper who spent years in the back of a drawer, His people did NOT.

cards.question: At the very end, the psalm writer names His people: Israel. How does he describe them?

answers.text: A people sent to the nations

cards.text: And the psalm ends right where it started: "Hallelujah!" He opened with it and closed with it, friend, with all of heaven and earth packed in between like a cookie box filled RIGHT up to the lid.
